args.summary: The latest release of checkout-api (v2.3.1) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an observed error rate of 18%. I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy status in production. Rollback applied per-region: us-east succeeded first; the initial rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, and a retry completed the rollback in us-west and eu-west. Service is now running v2.3.0 in all regions. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression (root cause of health check failures / 18% error rate) and the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout halt, before re-attempting a v2.3.1 release.

Done. Summary of what happened:

**Diagnosis**
- checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- Deployment history showed v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production.

**Rollback to v2.3.0**
- The first rollback attempt was a partial success: us-east rolled back, but the rollout halted with an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on the bad v2.3.1.
- I retried the rollback, which completed successfully — all three regions are now on v2.3.0.

**Incident**
- Opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001) for checkout-api describing the v2.3.1 health check failures, the rollback to v2.3.0, and the orchestrator error during the first rollback attempt. The create request reported a timeout, but I verified via the incident list that it was actually created — no duplicate was filed. On-call has been paged via this incident.

Remaining follow-ups noted in the incident: root-cause the v2.3.1 regression and the orchestrator rollout halt before re-attempting the v2.3.1 release.
